messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martin <alex.martin@bigbank.com>, ops@bigbank.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Dec 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: VPC deployment - bandwidth sizing, QoS policy, and peering handshake

Hi Alex / BigBank ops team,

Thanks again for the sync yesterday. As we start finalizing the private VPC handoff for the pilot, there are three items we need firm answers on before we lock the reference diagram and hand the runbook to Oncall:

1) Bandwidth profile: expected sustained egress per tenant (MB/s) and burst needs (95th percentile). We built a draft matrix (attached) using the pilot telemetry; please confirm the expected numbers for tile processing and embedding workloads.

2) Control plane QoS: we recommend reserving a small class for control-plane + KV cache replication (DSCP CS6) and a secondary for telemetry/logs. We need confirmation that your edge fabric can honor DSCP markings and per-flow policing.

3) Peering: BGP sessions, MD5 auth, and allowed ASNs. For the initial canary we propose: single BGP session per colo with backup session to a different PoP, /30 pairs, and explicit MTU 9000 on the data plane. If BigBank requires NAT hairpin avoidance we should add an asymmetric egress IP policy.

Attached: vpc-bandwidth-qos-matrix.xlsx (draft), reference-diagram-v2.pdf (annotated).

Target: I'd like to finalize the diagram and checklist by Friday so we can schedule the first canary on Monday. Please reply with the bandwidth numbers and whether your networking team can accept DSCP markers and jumbo MTU.

Thanks,
Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 24 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: VPC deployment - bandwidth sizing, QoS policy, and peering handshake

Sergio,

Thanks for the clear list. Quick answers from my side and a couple questions for the network team below:

- Bandwidth: For the pilot tenants we can commit to 250 Mbps sustained per tenant with 1 Gbps short bursts (90s). For the first 3 tenants this is fine; for production we should revisit (we have a dedicated egress pipe to the colo).

- DSCP: We can preserve DSCP; needs a config change in the edge switch fabric. Ops@ will confirm exact model and timeline.

- MTU: 9000 is OK in the colo but we have two intermediate ISP hops that currently reduce effective MTU to 8900. We can set PMTU and avoid fragmentation, but we need your runtime to support fallback to 1500 for peers that cannot do jumbo frames.

Peering: We prefer MD5 on BGP, ASN 64512 for BigBank edge; config for /30s is acceptable. One ask: can Redwood publish a static route for the control-plane management IPs so we can pin them for monitoring (we'll put them into our NMS).

I'll run the bandwidth numbers by ops and get you a confirmation by EOD. Also please drop the runbook link in Drive so I can invite my NOC.

Best,
Alex Martin
Network Engineering Lead, BigBank, Inc.
alex.martin@bigbank.com

Alex / Ops team,

Thanks — a few operational notes from the Redwood side based on your answers:

- Runtime MTU fallback: the inference runtime can fall back to 1500 on a per-peer basis. We'll make the change in the control-plane config so the data-plane path negotiates per-peer MTU on session start.

- Telemetry: we'll place high-cardinality traces on a non-priority queue. If you have a spare telemetry VLAN we can ensure those packets are out-of-band to limit impact on data-plane bursts.

- BGP MD5: agreed. We will publish three management IPs for the control plane behind a small anycast set; however, for NMS pinning we can provide the primary cluster leader IP and a contact alias (nms-contact@redwood.ai).

I've attached the updated reference diagram (reference-diagram-v2.pdf) with annotated VLANs and the suggested DSCP map. Please review the DSCP mapping in the bottom-right (CS6 for control, AF31 for retrieval bursts).

Action: Alex — can you confirm the exact switch model so we can provide a vendor-specific QoS recipe? Jonas/Kim — once Alex confirms, I'll update the runbook and tag SUP-4523.

Marissa

- We'll enable BGP MD5 as requested. Suggestion: set the hold-time to 90s for the initial canary (gives some tolerance for transient latency) and then harden to 30s for production.

Alex / team — thanks for the fast responses. Summary and next steps:

- BigBank confirmed pilot bandwidth (250 Mbps sustained / 1 Gbps burst). We'll mark that in the matrix and size the egress tunnel accordingly.
- DSCP preservation: agreed; Alex to confirm switch model (Alex: if you can paste the model + firmware I'll provide the vendor QoS recipe).
- MTU fallback: runtime will negotiate PMTU and fall back to 1500 per peer.
- BGP: MD5 + /30s + ASN 64512 accepted. Jonas to prepare checklist; Marissa to update runbook.

Plan: We'll finalize the reference diagram and the bgp-peering-checklist by Monday morning and schedule a 90-minute canary window for the first tenant on Tuesday. I'll add the runbook and checklist to the Drive link and tag SUP-4523 for the change window.

Happy holidays — appreciate the responsiveness over the break.

Sergio
